note: Sat 21 Nov 2026 07:xx SGT refresh, as of the Fri 20 Nov US close (latest completed session; markets closed for the weekend, no newer session for US/HK/SG/JP/KR). Friday was a SHARP, DISTINCT escalation, not a simple continuation of Thursday's Fed/Philly-Fed risk-off: S&P 500 -3.70% to 6910.39 (5th straight down day, confirming a correction from October highs), Nasdaq -5.28%, Russell 2000 -2.76%, VIX +26.2% to 35.89 (highest since March). The proximate triggers were two Friday-specific AI-credibility shocks -- Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining Nvidia's accounting practices (NVDA -14%, ~$500bn of market cap erased) and Ming-Chi Kuo reported Alphabet cut ~20% of its 2027 Broadcom-designed TPU orders in favor of MediaTek (AVGO -11.4%, MRVL -10%) -- landing on monthly options expiration day when ~55-57% of SPY/QQQ's negative gamma was rolling off, a structural amplifier that helps explain why VIX moved so much more than the index itself. Gold and silver fell in the SAME session as equities (GLD -3.67%, SLV -6.74%, GDX -5.00%, SILJ -5.89%) despite softer US data (final UoM sentiment rose to 51.5, inflation expectations fell to 3.7%/3.3%) -- analysts attribute this to a margin-call transmission mechanism (leveraged investors raising cash from liquid winners to meet equity-related calls) rather than a fresh metals-specific catalyst, consistent with COMEX managed-money futures positions shrinking even as ETF holdings rose. Rare earths gave back their 3-day rally (MP -7.39%, having rallied Nov 17-19 on US-China trade-talk optimism and a 3-insider cluster buy) as broad-market beta overwhelmed the idiosyncratic story. Bitcoin extended a separate, multi-week decline (-4.51% to $59,109) tied to ~$1.9bn of cumulative spot-ETF outflows, MSCI's removal of Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes, and thin weekend Coinbase-concentrated selling -- this looks like continuation of an existing drain, not a new Friday-specific shock. CNN Fear & Greed fell to 14 (Extreme Fear, from 19 Thursday), yet counterintuitively BofA/EPFR and Lipper's week-ended-18-Nov fund flows (published Nov 20, finally covering this entire selloff week) both showed net equity INFLOWS (+$66.6bn and +$59.2bn respectively) -- a genuine divergence between price action and fund-level flows worth flagging rather than reconciling into one narrative. Fed Governor Waller's Nov 18 call for a 'shock therapy' 50bp December hike, reinforced by Governor Cook's hawkish tone Nov 20, keeps the rate backdrop a second, independent headwind. All 40 universe calls plus the 9-ticker rare-earth basket were re-levelled this run; the largest-magnitude-move tickers got fresh ticker-specific drivers, the rest were nudged in the direction of the broad shock per house rule rather than re-invented without a fresh catalyst.

macro.regime: Hawkish Fed into AI-capex unwind / credit-stress risk-off
macro.narrative: Equities enter Monday ~9% below the Nov 11 high after Nvidia's SEC accounting probe (stock -50% from its October peak, interim CEO Colette Kress reining in vendor financing) crystallized the AI-capex unwind flagged by BofA's November Fund Manager Survey, which recorded the largest cut to tech overweights since June 2006 and 52% of managers expecting a hyperscaler capex cut within six months. Markets price ~90-95% odds of a 25bp Fed hike on Dec 9 (Dallas Fed's Logan wants two more; Waller's 50bp 'shock' push has been partly priced out after Treasury Secretary Bessent warned Sunday the Fed risks overtightening). Credit stress is widening underneath, not complacent: HY OAS +29bp this week to 352bp with CCC spreads blowing out above 1000bp over Treasuries (AI-linked credit such as CoreWeave trading at distressed levels), while IG spreads widened only +5bp to 94bp -- stress is concentrated at the bottom of the credit stack, not yet systemic. China eased margin rules and Taiwan deployed a NT$500bn stabilization fund after the TAIEX's worst week in 35 years, both targeted liquidity responses rather than a change in the underlying AI-capex-credibility problem. Levels as of Fri 20 Nov US close; weekend/Monday-morning developments (Bessent's dovish pushback, China/Taiwan stabilization measures, a fresh Hormuz shipping escalation) are incorporated qualitatively above pending Monday's Asia/US sessions.
